theme: 3 terms on switching over enums safely: covering every case, preparing for cases added later, and enums that promise never to change

terms.definition: A `switch` that covers every possible case, so it needs no `default`.
terms.example: Keep it an Exhaustive Switch, so the compiler tells us about new cases.

terms.definition: A case written `@unknown default` that handles enum cases added in the future but still warns about current ones you missed.
terms.example: Add an Unknown Default, because Apple may add new states later.

terms.definition: A public enum marked `@frozen` that promises it will never get new cases.
terms.example: `Optional` is a Frozen Enum, so two cases are always enough.

video.title: Exhaustive Switch, Unknown Default & Frozen Enum | Day 51
video.description:
Learn to explain safe switches over enums in Swift: Exhaustive Switch, Unknown Default & Frozen Enum, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Exhaustive Switch - A `switch` that covers every possible case, so it needs no `default`.
Unknown Default - A case written `@unknown default` that handles enum cases added in the future but still warns about current ones you missed.
Frozen Enum - A public enum marked `@frozen` that promises it will never get new cases.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.title: Swift Exhaustive Switch, Unknown Default & Frozen Enum | Day 51
landscape.description:
Explain Exhaustive Switch, Unknown Default & Frozen Enum in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
완전한 스위치, 언노운 디폴트, 프로즌 열거형 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Exhaustive Switch - A `switch` that covers every possible case, so it needs no `default`.
한국어: 완전한 스위치: 가능한 모든 case를 다뤄서 default가 필요 없는 switch

Unknown Default - A case written `@unknown default` that handles enum cases added in the future but still warns about current ones you missed.
한국어: 언노운 디폴트: @unknown default로 쓰며, 나중에 추가될 case를 처리하면서 지금 빠뜨린 case는 경고해 주는 case

Frozen Enum - A public enum marked `@frozen` that promises it will never get new cases.
한국어: 프로즌 열거형: @frozen을 붙여 앞으로 새 case가 절대 추가되지 않는다고 약속하는 public enum

In this video, Mina and Jake sort out why a switch over Apple's enum needs an extra case, why a plain default is worse and which enums never change, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.
Mina와 Jake의 채팅 스타일 대화와 화면 속 Swift 코드로 배워요.

landscape.hook: Can you explain safe enum switches in English?

dialogue.title: All four cases, still not enough?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, why does this `switch` need `@unknown default`? I covered all four cases.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Today, yes. But Apple can add a new thermal state later.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And my Exhaustive Switch would break?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. An Unknown Default catches cases that don't exist yet.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: With an Unknown Default, the compiler still warns you when a new case appears.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nice. Do I need it for `Optional` too?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No. `Optional` is a Frozen Enum. It promises never to get new cases.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So for a Frozen Enum, an Exhaustive Switch is enough.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. Exhaustive Switch for my enums, Unknown Default for Apple's, Frozen Enum for promises.
An Exhaustive Switch needs no default at all.
